messages.subject: model averaging Error
messages.body_plain:
Hi all
I would like to  do model averaging of two best models
mod1=  (D~1 g0~h2 sigma~h2 pmix~h2)
mod2 = (D~1 a0~h2 sigma~h2 pmix~h2)
As we can see the detection parameters are not same hence in these two models, hence I only selected (D,sigma and pmix) as real and beta parameter.
But I find this error.
 m<-model.average(mod1, mod2, realnames = c("D","sigma","pmix"),betanames = c("D","sigma",pmix))
Error in model.average(mod1, mod2, realnames = c("D", "sigma", "pmix"),  :
  'model.average' cannot handle scaled detection parameters
Could you guide me how to do model averaging for these two models as there AIC differences are less than two.
,

messages.subject: Re: model averaging Error
messages.body_plain:
Hello Mayank

You've probably figured this out for yourself by now, but...

Firstly, the two models are the same and it makes no sense to average them. Using the 'captdata' dataset:
AIC(mod1, mod2)
                          model   detectfn npar    logLik      AIC     AICc dAICc AICcwt
mod1 D~1 g0~h2 sigma~h2 pmix~h2 halfnormal    6 -758.4792 1528.958 1530.176     0    0.5
mod2 D~1 a0~h2 sigma~h2 pmix~h2 halfnormal    6 -758.4792 1528.958 1530.176     0    0.5

This is because you make a0 unique to each mixture class (a0~h2) rather than constant (a0~1).

Secondly, model.average() does not handle the a0 parameterisation or 'scaled detection parameters' as they used to be called. If you want to average such models you have to do it by hand.

Thirdly, do not specify both realnames and betanames as arguments of model.average(). The help says "To average beta parameters, specify betanames (this is ignored if a value is provided for realnames)."

Murray

messages.subject_clean: Error in uniroot & Error in naivecap2
messages.body_plain:
Hello Marie-Lyne
The error you report is coming from the initial 'autoini' step, when secr.fit finds starting values for the likelihood maximization. I'm guessing your data are limited in some way (no recaptures at different sites?), or the mask is inappropriate; I admit the message is not informative. If you have checked the data and the mask (plotting is always helpful) the next step is to override the automatic starting values by specifying them yourself (e.g., start = list(D=2, g0=0.1, sigma=30) where D is in animals/ha and sigma is in metres).
Murray

P.S. The idea of covnames is to provide informative labels of your choice - perhaps you can do better than V5?

messages.subject: fx.total error
messages.body_plain:
Hello all, I have what I hope will be an easy question. I am trying to produce a surface of coyote activity centers using fx.total() and I am getting an error that I can't figure out. here is the simple line of code that I have tried to run and the error it produces:

> fxsurface <- fx.total(foxs_null, sessnum=2)

Error in fx.total(foxs_null, sessnum = 2) : not for ms model

At first I thought that the "ms" might mean multisession, but you can see that I added in the sessnum argument and still got the error. Anyone know what this error is trying to tell me? Thanks!

Casey

messages.subject: Re: fx.total error
messages.body_plain:
Hi Casey
'ms' really does refer to multisession models (there's even a function ms that tests for whether a model fit or capthist object is multisession). What you stumbled on was an inconsistency in the code: it seemed to let you specify a sessnum for multisession data, then spat it out if you tried. Whoever wrote this **** didn't finish the job. I have rushed through a change that should make it work as expected (see working version 2.9.6 at www.otago.ac.nz/density/SECRinR.html <http://www.otago.ac.nz/density/SECRinR.html>). At least I can do
library(secr)
fxsurface <- fx.total(ovenbird.model.D, sessnum=3)
plot(fxsurface, covariate = 'D.sum')

and get a meaningful plot, or at least as meaningful as one ever gets from fx.total. Note the need to specify covariate = 'D.sum' (the default D.0 fails).
Thanks for reporting this, and let me know if there are further problems.
Murray
